about: Stop 9 on the map page: Etemenanki seen across its precinct's court from Gate 5, in UTM metres (E, N) and German-zero levels like map-plan.json. The precinct's east wall keeps the map's line, thickness and Gate 5 gap; the recess, the store blocks, the street's paving and the tower's faces are drawn here. Every height and finish above the dug plans is guessed, and says so.

gate5.src: an opening about 30 m wide between the two east store buildings (P2021 p. 211); its centre read off C6.2 at about 445964.5, 3600121.5 on the wall's outer face, the recess's sides about 30 m apart; its depth not known: C6.2 draws an inner cross wall about 70 to 75 m in, drawn, not dug
gate5.axis: the recess runs in square to the map's wall line (254.1 grid; the sheet's read-off is about 255, inside its error)
gate5.inner: the gate at the recess's inner end was totally destroyed (P2021 p. 209 to 211): no gate body, no height, no facade; its place is a threshold course across the recess's end, guessed

wall.src: the map's line and 8 m thickness (C6.2); a mud-brick double wall with slight towers, two store buildings with deep chambers against the east side (K1914 ch. XXX)
wall.hsrc: the walls' height, the towers' pitch, width and rise are ours (bab.precinct.body, guessed; the rhythm of slight towers after Koldewey's drawing of 1919); white lime-gypsum plaster over mud brick as one model shows it (P2021 fig. 4.19 caption), guessed

south.towers: the east wall's slight towers (wall.towers) on the south rooms' street face, the first a half pitch and 4 m from each end of a run, as the east wall's: their spacing, width, projection and rise are ours (bab.precinct.body, guessed); a double wall with slight towers (K1914 ch. XXX)

square.src: the south side had gates with open squares 21 x 25 m before them (P2021 p. 208): Gate 8's square where C6.2 cuts the south rooms between 445677 and 445698 E (precinct sheet 1.3 reads 21 x 27 m), the map's 21 m gap; 25 m deep from the street face, the gate across its inner end; the recess's sides carry the slight towers as Gate 5's do (ours)

gate.src: the gate across the square's inner end, in the rooms' remaining 7 m: its form is not known, all ours (G): two flanking masses risen 4 m over the wall, the middle over the passage 1.2 m lower and 0.4 m back, a passage 4.2 m wide after the cross street at Gate 5 (P2021 p. 209 to 213) and 7.5 m high; the masses 0.4 m proud of the court face

breccia.src: the west and middle 4.2 m in reddish breccia slabs about 59 by 59 cm, seven across (P2021 p. 209 to 213)

brick.src: the east 2.2 m in brick laid in asphalt (P2021 p. 209 to 213)

street.margin: the map's street is 8.6 m wide; the dug 6.4 m lies on its middle, the rest is the street's unpaved shoulder, guessed
street.splitSrc: the paving as dug at the main entrance (bab.street.south-paved) to 30 m south of the opening's axis; south of that the street to the corner was reached only in a few trenches (bab.street.precinct-east, guessed)

cross.src: a perpendicular street 4.2 m wide led from the Processional Way into the precinct (P2021 p. 209 to 213); drawn on C6.2 along the recess's middle; its paving not described, brick here, guessed

panels.src: the first stage 'indented or ornamented with buttresses' (Smith's reading of the tablet, K1914 ch. XXX); about 13 tall panels a side in Pedersén's model (P2021 fig. 4.18): the panels, their depth and the upper stages' panels are ours (bab.tower.wallface, guessed; the rhythm after Koldewey's restored tower of 1919)

stairMass.src: the side stairs' masses carry the first stage's panels on their outer faces, in the rhythm of the stage face behind them and at its depth, as the mantle the masses were painted with before; each recess's head level under the flight's line by the stages' band (coping and drip), none shorter than it is wide (ours, bab.tower.wallface, guessed)

forms.src: the panels built as relief at panels.pitch1, share and out: the recesses sunk 0.5 m into the stage's side, so the measured side stays the panels' face, none in the end bays; a coping on every stage's top, four courses high, a brick's length out over the panels, its underside hung two courses below the panels' heads as its drip, so the rain fell clear of the face (the coping, its lip and drip ours, bab.tower.wallface, guessed: the record is silent on the stages' tops); the arrises left sharp: a soft arris of a few cm is under a pixel at every stop
forms.seen: the 3 px rule (forge test): each form's size times the px per metre of the stop that shows it, from pxm.py on the walk's cameras: S09 13.9 (299 m, desktop and phone), S12 21 to 24 desktop and 24 to 29 phone on the stage faces

stairs.src: the middle stair and the two side stairs where the map draws them, up to the first stage's top (P2021 p. 156); their steps are ours, about 30 cm risers, drawn in the material on the stair's slope (bab.tower.stair.middle.rise, bab.tower.stairs.side.rise, guessed)

middle.src: 10.2 m wide outside, walls about 2 m, 6.2 m clear (P2021 p. 156; bab.tower.stair.middle): a flight between two side walls; the walls' height over the flight is ours, 1 m

side.src: the west side stair's foot lies 1.9 m west of the tower (P2021 p. 156), so its first step stands there at the court's level; the east one's the same, ours by symmetry; 8 m wide and climbing along the south face to the first stage's top where the map draws them (P2021 p. 156); a wall 1.2 m thick on each one's outer edge, its top 1 m over the steps' nosings, ours
side.ledgeSrc: the stair's mass carries the mantle's panels up to its flight's line, and the parapet in the stair's brick stands on it 0.3 m back, stepping with the treads: the setback, the stepped top and the panels on the stair's side are ours
side.steps: built as steps, a riser and a tread each: 110 risers of 0.3 m on treads of about 0.38 m (the risers ours, bab.tower.stairs.side.rise, guessed); the inner edge runs 0.1 m into the tower's face
side.landing: where the three meet: each side stair's head runs on level at the first stage's top to the middle flight's edge (about 2.65 m), its parapet level over it, and the middle stair's walls end against the side stairs' outer face, so the middle flight climbs its last 8.5 m between the two landings; the landing's form is not known, ours

temple.src: the king says he raised Etemenanki's top with baked bricks of shining blue glaze (RIBo Nebuchadnezzar II 002 iii 15); no such fragment was found at Babylon (P2021 p. 162): blue, guessed (bab.tower.topglaze); the hue is ours, no colour source for the tower's glaze exists, taken inside the gate's measured cobalt range

door.src: one door in the face toward the stairs; its size and place are ours (bab.tower.top: the top building's form is not known)

crest.src: stepped battlements round the roof as the gate and the walls carry them (the battlements part); on the temple they are ours

temple.colourSrc: linear albedo, ours: CIELAB hue 277, chroma 29, a fifth of the white's lightness, inside the gate's measured cobalt (hue 264 to 284, 0.08 to 0.22 of the white) at its light end, so the glaze in shade stays blue

tower.brick: baked brick 32 by 32 or 31.5 cm in bitumen, unstamped (P2021 p. 155): the bond and the tone are ours

air.src: the spring air's extinction over the plain, ours: about 8 percent of the light between the gate and the tower's face is the sunlit haze's (a visual range of about 15 km); the haze takes the horizon sky's colour toward the view, the sun's glow included

colours.src: linear albedo, ours: the baked brick from the gate kit's buff and red-brown (PAL), tinted toward the yellow-buff of Babylon's unglazed brick; the white plaster warm and matte (an open plaster scan's look, tinted); the mud brick at the walls' foot where splash wore the plaster; the court's earth the plain's dust

door.opens: the tower you can measure (feature 7), a close look on paper: src/wings/babylon/measure/
door.src: the stop's one press, named by what it shows and never 'Learn more' (the words are the writer's); it stands clear of the tower in both framings, on the court at the lower right of the wide frame and on the cross street under the tower in the upright one, so the frame at rest keeps far more than two thirds picture

dug.about: the switch's second state: the tower as excavated, not the state of 570 BC (bab.tower.ruin, In place, not of the date); the precinct round it stays as it was about 570 BC

core.src: a core of unbaked mud brick about 60 by 60 m, its top today about +2.0 to +2.5 (P2021 p. 155); its eroded sides' slope ours

trench.src: the mantle about 15 m thick, founded at -4.0 (P2021 p. 155), robbed for its bricks from 1886, leaving a deep cut round the core (P2021 p. 153; K1914 ch. XXX): the floor at the mantle's foundation, the banks' slope and the debris on the floor ours

water.src: the cut is often water-filled (P2021 p. 153, fig. 4.14 caption): its level and its look ours

stairs.src: the three stairs' foundations as dug: the middle stair's two walls to its foot 105.3 m from the centre, the side stairs' band 45.6 to 53.4 m from the centre, the west foot 1.9 m beyond the tower (P2021 p. 156); drawn as their walls' tops just proud of the ground, the band's part over the robbers' bank left out; their level as dug is not given, ours

dug.look: the photograph of the ruin today (Verburg 2012, CC0) for the look only, never as a texture
